claim: Anthropic introduced and open-sourced MCP as a standard for connecting AI assistants to external data systems on 2024-11-25.
notes: Primary announcement; used only for origin and stated motivation.

claim: MCP follows a Host–Client–Server architecture; a Host can manage multiple clients, and servers expose focused capabilities.
locator: Architecture overview; participants and design principles

claim: MCP servers expose Tools, Resources and Prompts as distinct primitives with different interaction models.
notes: Current specification; exact methods and lifecycle are version-scoped.

claim: MCP supports local STDIO and remote Streamable HTTP transports; transport is distinct from the JSON-RPC data layer.
The 2026-07-28 specification removes initialize/initialized and Mcp-Session-Id from the stateless core; requests carry version and client metadata, and server/discover is optional.
locator: The 2026-07-28 Specification; What changed; No handshake or sessions
notes: Official specification release article by MCP maintainers.

claim: 2026-07-28 adds Multi Round-Trip Requests, Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name routing headers and cache hints including ttlMs/cacheScope.
locator: MRTR; Header-based routing; List results are cacheable

claim: Tasks moved from experimental core functionality to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension, with task handles and tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel.
notes: Current extension lifecycle; not every client supports every extension.

claim: MCP authorization requires audience-bound token validation; token passthrough is forbidden, and the 2026-07-28 revision hardens issuer validation and moves away from DCR toward CIMD.
locator: Token Passthrough and authorization security guidance
notes: Official security guidance; implementation must follow OAuth security best practices.

claim: Confused deputy, token passthrough, prompt injection and tool poisoning are relevant risks in MCP deployments.
locator: Key Risks: Tool Poisoning, Rug Pull, Tool Shadowing; Prompt Injection via Tool Return Values
notes: OWASP MCP Security Cheat Sheet; use alongside official MCP authorization guidance.

claim: OpenAI Responses API can connect remote MCP servers and private/local servers via Secure MCP Tunnel, with approval, tool filtering and deferred tool loading controls.
locator: MCP servers; Secure MCP Tunnel; Filtering tools; Approval and risks
notes: Current OpenAI developer documentation; API details may evolve.

claim: OWASP recommends least privilege, scoped credentials, short-lived tokens and integrity review of tool definitions.
The N×M versus N+M integration comparison is a simplified conceptual model of bespoke versus shared-protocol adapter structure, not a measured benchmark.
locator: Original announcement: fragmented integrations and custom implementation motivation
notes: Independent teaching abstraction; no empirical cost or latency claim.

claim: The Python example models Host-side allow-list, schema and approval checks plus a 2026-07-28-shaped JSON-RPC request; it is not a complete MCP implementation.
locator: Base protocol and tools/call; teaching adapter code
notes: Tested invariants are local demonstrations only, not conformance or security certification.

claim: Tool descriptions and schemas can be poisoned or changed after approval; cross-server tool shadowing and prompt injection via tool return values require definition integrity checks and independent authorization.
locator: Key Risks; Tool Description & Schema Integrity; Prompt Injection via Tool Return Values
notes: OWASP MCP Security Cheat Sheet; recommendations are defense-in-depth practices, not guarantees.

claim: Under the stateless 2026-07-28 model, application state may be represented by explicit handles; servers must not treat possession as authentication and should bind handles to authenticated users, use unpredictable values and enforce expiry.
notes: Official MCP security guidance for the stateless protocol revision.

claim: The 2026-07-28 revision requires issuer validation per RFC 9207, binds client credentials to the issuing authorization server, and formally deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents while preserving backward compatibility.
MCP 2026-07-28 tools support full JSON Schema 2020-12 inputSchema and outputSchema; structuredContent can be any JSON value, with output validation and bounded schema processing.
notes: The release-candidate article documents SEP-2106, incorporated in the final 2026-07-28 revision.
